newsitem.title: CANADA: Maple Leaf lays off 100 at Winnipeg plant.
newsitem.headline: Maple Leaf lays off 100 at Winnipeg plant.

text.p: Maple Leaf Foods Inc, Canada's largest food processor, issued 100 layoff notices to workers at its Winnipeg hog kill plant on Monday, United Food and Commercial Workers' union spokesman Don Keith said.
The layoffs come as the result of protracted negotiations between Maple Leaf pork processing unit Burns Meats Ltd and hog marketer Manitoba Pork.
Manitoba Pork, which markets more than 80 percent of hogs produced in Manitoba, scrapped its one-price-for-all formula January 31 when its contract with Burns and three other processors expired.

Manitoba Agriculture Minister Harry Enns brokered an agreement February 6 in which Manitoba Pork reinstituted the old formula until February 21 in hopes it and the processors could agree on a new pricing regime.
The negotiations between the processors and Manitoba Pork continued all day Monday, Manitoba Government spokesman Roger Matas said.
An agreement may still be reached but layoff notices issued at Manitoba's largest processor, Burns, which employs 800 workers, indicated that daily production runs may be scaled back.
An average of between 6,500 to 7,000 hogs are slaughtered daily in Manitoba.
